topic: California petition for change of name
statement: In California you change your legal name by filing a Petition for Change of Name (Form NC-100) and related forms in the superior court for the county where you live.
detail: The court issues a decree of change of name that you then use to update other documents. If you cannot afford the filing fee, you can request a fee waiver with Form FW-001.

cost.note: The filing fee varies by county (commonly around $435–$480); a fee waiver is available if you cannot afford it.

timeline.typical: roughly 6–12 weeks from filing to a signed order

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Change Your Name

topic: California petition for change of gender
statement: California lets you petition for a court recognition of a change of gender and sex identifier, and you can request a name change in the same set of forms.
detail: You do not need to give any medical documentation to get a court order recognizing a gender change, or to change California state-issued documents. You can ask for a gender marker of female, male, or nonbinary.

cost.note: The filing fee is $435–$450. If you cannot afford it, you can ask the court to waive it.

timeline.typical: about two months; a judge decides in about 1 to 2 months

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Change Your Legal Gender

statement: To change the name on your California driver's license or ID, visit the DMV with proof of your legal name change, such as your court order, and apply for a replacement card.

cost.note: A replacement card fee applies; check the current DMV fee schedule.

timeline.typical: a temporary card is issued at the visit; the permanent card arrives by mail

source.title: California DMV — Driver's Licenses & ID Cards

statement: California lets you pick a gender category of male (M), female (F), or nonbinary (X) on your driver's license or ID card. You use the DMV's online application to apply for a new card with the updated gender category.
detail: The DMV says your gender category change is not complete until you come into a field office. The DMV page no longer names a paper Gender Category Request form; it routes the change through the online DL/ID application instead. Be ready to pay the appropriate licensing fee.

cost.note: The DMV page does not list a separate gender-category fee. It says to be ready to pay the appropriate licensing fee.

timeline.typical: not complete until you visit a DMV field office

source.title: California DMV — Update Information on Your Driver's License or ID Card

statement: If you were born in California, you can change the sex field on your birth record to reflect your gender identity by mailing in form VS 24B, the Application to Amend a Birth Record.
detail: California Vital Records takes all birth amendment requests by mail. The amendment page does not state a fee or a processing time. It links to the current fee page and the current processing-time page instead.

source.title: California Department of Public Health — Amending a California Birth Record

topic: California birth certificate: no court order needed
statement: In California you can change the gender marker or sex identifier on a birth certificate without a court order and without medical certification.
detail: The state courts' self-help guide says to update (amend) your California birth certificate through the California Department of Public Health.

source.title: California Courts Self-Help — Update your gender marker or sex identifier on your identity documents

statement: To change the name on a California birth record after a court order, mail in form VS 23, the Application to Amend a Birth Certificate After a Court Order Name Change.
detail: You need the signed court order first. California Vital Records takes all birth amendment requests by mail, and it will ask you for more paperwork if your request is short of what it needs.

source.title: California Department of Public Health — Amending a California Birth Record

statement: California's fee list shows a $26 fee to amend a birth record. It covers a court-order name change (form VS 23) and a change to the sex field, and it includes one free copy of the new record.
detail: The fee to change or correct the sex field is $26 no matter when you ask for it. Extra certified copies of a California birth record cost $31 each. Pay by check or money order, not cash.

cost.note: Includes one free copy of the amended record. Extra certified copies are $31 each.

source.title: California Department of Public Health — Vital Records Fees
